claims.text: Myelosuppression (anemia, leukopenia, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia), reverses on stopping.
claims.quote: Myelosuppression (including anemia, leukopenia, pancytopenia, and thrombocytopenia) has been reported in patients receiving linezolid. In cases where the outcome is known, when linezolid was discontinued, the affected hematologic parameters have risen toward pretreatment levels.

claims.text: Peripheral and optic neuropathy, mainly beyond 28 days.
claims.quote: Peripheral and optic neuropathies have been reported in patients treated with ZYVOX, primarily in those patients treated for longer than the maximum recommended duration of 28 days.

claims.text: Hypoglycemia in diabetics on insulin or oral agents.
claims.quote: Hypoglycemia: Postmarketing cases of symptomatic hypoglycemia have been reported in patients with diabetes mellitus receiving insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents.
Myelosuppression: Monitor complete blood counts weekly.

claims.text: Prompt eye exam for visual symptoms.
claims.quote: If patients experience symptoms of visual impairment, prompt ophthalmic evaluation is recommended.

claims.text: Any MAOI now or within two weeks.
claims.quote: Patients taking any monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI) or within two weeks of taking an MAOI.

claims.text: Serotonin syndrome (including fatal) with SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, buspirone, triptans, opioids incl. meperidine.
claims.quote: Spontaneous reports of serotonin syndrome including fatal cases associated with the concomitant use of ZYVOX and serotonergic agents have been reported. Commonly used serotonergic agents include serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, buspirone, serotonin 5‑HT1 receptor agonists (triptans), and opioids, including meperidine.

claims.text: Enhanced pressor response with pseudoephedrine and other indirect sympathomimetics, vasopressors or dopaminergic drugs.
claims.quote: Some individuals receiving ZYVOX may experience a reversible enhancement of the pressor response to indirect-acting sympathomimetic agents, vasopressor or dopaminergic agents. Commonly used drugs such as phenylpropanolamine and pseudoephedrine have been specifically studied.

claims.text: Avoid large amounts of high-tyramine foods/drinks (aged, fermented, pickled or smoked, eg aged cheeses).
claims.quote: Advise patients to avoid large quantities of foods or beverages with high tyramine content while taking ZYVOX. Foods high in tyramine content include those that may have undergone protein changes by aging, fermentation, pickling, or smoking to improve flavor, such as aged cheeses
